title: 3-round AES single-key differential-linear distinguisher, |C|=2^-7.66

target.description: Figure3: three SubBytes layers R0,R1,R2, with SR/MC/AK between layers, input difference before R0 SB and output mask immediately after R2 SB. No general final-MC/other-endpoint equivalence is assumed. AppendixC Fig9b/Table5 gives an equivalent explicit full-SR/MC output mask: row-major0032000000ab00000066000000980000 pulls back by the binary transpose of SR/MC to byte(row2,col3)=0x67 at the Fig3 last-SB endpoint. This checked mapping applies to this pattern, not arbitrary endpoint conventions.

setting.key_relation: One fixed unknown key; no related-key queries or round-key control.
setting.key_population: single-secret-key AES of all key sizes under the source differential-linear correlation model
setting.plaintext_model: Chosen pairs with a fixed input difference and fixed output linear mask. AppendixC Table5 row-major serialization: DeltaX0=0000000000000000000000000000b400, GammaX3=0032000000ab00000066000000980000; ru=0,rm=3,rl=0;p=q=1,r=2^-7.66.
setting.reference_model: Differential-linear output-parity statistic versus a random permutation; source correlation is not decision probability or advantage.
assumptions: Generalized DLCT handles middle dependency; outer composition uses the source prq^2 correlation model.
Source endpoint/trail conventions remain explicit; affine output layers are not silently treated as identical endpoints.
The published generalized-DLCT composition assumes round/round-key independence and averaged random-key correlations; exact correlation for every fixed standard AES master key is not established.

Published author README additionally gives a three-round(b4,67) reproduction recipe with2^25 random-base pair queries under each of10 random fixed master keys. Its sample signed counts are negative and reported average magnitude is2^-7.6748. The recipe is not assumed to describe every Table2 experiment or to provide fixed-key confidence bounds.

success.description: The3-round AES point reports absolute differential-linear correlation |C|=2^-7.66, not a finite-budget distinguishing decision probability. The round-independence approximation concerns the random-key average, not a guarantee for every fixed key. Table2 reports the best pair (b4,67) with theoretical signed correlation -2^-7.66 and experimental -2^-7.64; neither is a repeated-trial decision-success rate. No per-point sample budget N, threshold or false-positive/false-negative distribution is specified. Keep signed correlation/theoretical support separate; do not relabel the correlation as a probability component or transfer a3-round experiment to other points.
